A compiled reference answers two questions: **which organizations** can a
record be matched to, and **which names and addresses** does each one carry.
Layers answer the first. Name and address classes answer the second; see
`vignette("corroborators")` and `vignette("sources")`.

Every EIN in matchdb has exactly one layer, so choosing layers is choosing a
clean set of EINs. Two layers never overlap, and their union is just more EINs.

## The layers

The counts are from the build of 2026-10-23 (`matchdb@bb68531`).

| layer | what it holds | EINs |
|---|---|---:|
| `bmf_active` | in the newest IRS Business Master File release | 1,974,830 |
| `bmf_inactive` | in an earlier BMF release, but not the newest: dissolved, merged, revoked or lapsed | 1,723,367 |
| `approved_only` | approved on Form 1023-EZ but never in a BMF release the database loaded | 12,581 |
| `filer_only` | never in the BMF, but seen in the e-file data: as a 990 filer, or as an EIN another filer reported on Schedule I or Schedule R | 318,389 |
| `postcard_only` | known only from the 990-N e-Postcard (small organizations) | 73,503 |
| `revoked_only` | known only from the IRS automatic-revocation list | 133,572 |
| `irs527` | political organizations from Form 8871 (defined; not loaded in this build) | 0 |

An EIN gets the layer of the **first** source, in build order, that
introduced it: the BMF, then 1023-EZ approvals, then the e-file data, then
the e-Postcard, then revocations. An organization that is in the BMF and also
files a 990-N is `bmf_active`, not `postcard_only`. Its e-Postcard names are
still in the database, as names on a `bmf_active` EIN.

## Layer is where an EIN came from; `active` is its status

`layer` records provenance and does not change once assigned. `entity.active`
records status, and only `bmf_active` EINs are active. Keeping the two apart
lets a new BMF release flip an organization's status without rewriting where
it came from.

## Choosing layers

`md_spec()` takes the layers to include:

```{r}
library(matchdb)

# the default: organizations in the current BMF
active <- md_spec(layers = "bmf_active")

# every EIN the BMF has ever listed
unified <- md_spec(layers = c("bmf_active", "bmf_inactive"))
```

Which to use depends on the records being matched.

- **Current records** (this year's grants, a current directory): `bmf_active`.
  The inactive tranche is nearly as large and adds little. In the 0c
  measurement it added 1.76M rows for **−5 YES** on the 1k grant benchmark,
  because a dissolved organization rarely receives this year's grant and its
  name competes with the live one.
- **Historical records** (grants from 2012, an old survey frame): add
  `bmf_inactive`, since the organization may have closed since.
- **Small organizations** that never filed a full 990: consider
  `postcard_only` and `revoked_only`. Most organizations that lose exemption
  are revoked for failing to file for three years, so many are small.
- **Recipients that are not in the BMF at all**, such as some government
  units, churches that never applied, and EINs reported by other filers:
  `filer_only`.

The published tiers use the two common choices: `active-*` is `bmf_active`,
and `unified-*` is `bmf_active` plus `bmf_inactive`.

## What a layer choice leaves out

A narrow layer choice can split a family. A chapter may be `bmf_inactive`
while its parent is `bmf_active`. `md_compile()` reports this in its absence
report: for each cluster type, how many family members the chosen layers
left out.

```{r}
r <- md_compile(md_spec(layers = "bmf_active"))
r$report$absence
```

## Looking at one EIN

`md_lookup()` shows an EIN's layer and everything else known about it:

```{r}
md_lookup("53-0196605")
#> <md_lookup> EIN-53-0196605  AMERICAN NATIONAL RED CROSS
#>   layer bmf_active, active TRUE, NTEE P210, subsection 3
#>   names      1800 rows (dba 1, in_care_of 1, legal 2, observed 1796)
#>   ...
```

`md_layers()` returns the vocabulary. It is append-only: values are added,
never renamed, so a stored layer never changes meaning.
